references.text: Pharaoh previously gave an order not to give straw to the Israelites, which directly leads to the command in verse 11 that they must gather it themselves.
The consequences of the demand to maintain production without straw are shown here, where the foremen are beaten because the people failed to meet the quota.
Repeats the same demand: no straw shall be given, but the same amount of bricks must be delivered.
Describes the harsh forced labor imposed on the Israelites in Egypt, including work with bricks and clay, which is the background for the oppression in chapter 5.
God sees the suffering of the Israelites under their taskmasters, which is reflected in the harsh demand in this verse.
Theological contrast between unpaid forced labor and the call to continue with hope in God's reward.
Contrast between denied straw in Exodus (oppression) and permitted gleaning of stalks/straw in Ruth (grace).
Thematic parallel about work that yields no pay or food due to oppression (Ex) or God's judgment (Hag).
